Eagle Scout Service Project

A Shed and Accessible Sink for Animal Assisted Happiness

I led Scouts and adult volunteers in building a shed structure and replacing an outdoor sink at Animal Assisted Happiness.

Dates
January–February 2024
Beneficiary
Animal Assisted Happiness
My Role
Planning, budgeting & construction leadership
Total Work Hours
Approximately 229 hours
On This PageProject OverviewPlanning & Design ChangesConstructionLeadership & ChallengesResults & Lessons Learned
01 / Overview

Project Overview

The farm needed a covered space for a washer and dryer to clean animal bedding and a handwashing station that people with disabilities could use. I drew the plans, researched materials and accessibility requirements, and set the budget.

02 / Planning

Planning & Design Changes

I first proposed an open shedrow with four posts and a roof for storage. When the farm asked for a laundry space, I revised the 8 × 10 ft plan to include a floor and framing for two walls. I updated the material list, cost estimate, and work schedule. I also used redwood and post-base brackets based on feedback about reducing the risk of rot.

03 / Construction

Construction

I broke the revised build into stages. We marked and dug the post holes, leveled the brackets, and poured concrete before setting the posts and building the floor, wall framing, and roof. We also removed the old sink and installed the replacement sink, countertop, and supports.

I showed volunteers how to do their jobs and explained the hazards before they started. My plan called for a safety briefing each workday, closed-toe shoes, and a first-aid kit within reach. We planned for safety glasses, gloves, and hearing protection as needed and kept loose clothing and long hair clear of drills. I assigned cutting to adults and planned for Scouts to measure, dig, and drill under adult supervision.

04 / Leadership

Leadership & Challenges

The expanded scope gave me more jobs to coordinate. Early on, I had trouble stepping back and letting others do the work. As the build went on, I assigned jobs that could run at the same time and scheduled younger Scouts for days with work they could do. That helped me delegate individual tasks while keeping the whole workday moving.

05 / Results

Results & Lessons Learned

My team completed the structural work and sink installation within the available funds and without injuries. The beneficiary finished the shed enclosure and connected the sink plumbing afterward.

Some jobs took longer than I estimated, so we stayed later to finish within the planned number of workdays. I learned to leave more room in the schedule for jobs that might take longer than expected.
